reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and all key premises—especially the strain-accommodation role of interfaces, the effect of nanocrystallinity on hysteresis, and the retention of entropy change—are specific claims about material behavior that require experimental support but are presented without any cited passages.
premises: First-order magnetostructural transition in FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs is hysteretic due to internal stress buildup
Microstructural interfaces can accommodate strain during a magnetostructural transition
Nanocrystalline grain structure can be induced by rapid annealing and quenching
Increased grain boundary density reduces hysteresis without significantly diminishing entropy change
The proposed mechanism applies to non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs under low-field magnetic cooling
